venue.name: Legacy Maltwood Art Museum & Gallery (UVic)
venue.description: Legacy Maltwood is the University of Victoria's gallery space on the Gordon Head campus, on the lower level of the Mearns Centre, McPherson Library. It is one of the two exhibition spaces run by UVic Legacy Art Galleries, the university's art museum, alongside Legacy Downtown. Admission is free and gallery hours follow the McPherson Library's hours. Free exhibition introductions for school classes and community groups of all ages are booked through the same email address as the downtown gallery.
venue.address: Lower level of the Mearns Centre, McPherson Library, University of Victoria, Victoria BC

facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Legacy Maltwood is located on the bottom level of the McPherson Library and can be accessed by stairs or elevator. There are no additional doors to enter the gallery; however, the layout of the space may be difficult for some mobility devices to navigate. For more information, please contact Library staff at 250 721-6673.

venue.hours_notes: Gallery hours are the same as those of the McPherson Library, which publishes its hours on the UVic Libraries locations page.

programs.name: Group visit with exhibition introduction
programs.description: A group visit to the current exhibitions with a short introduction from gallery staff. Offered free to university classes, school classes and community groups of all ages. To book, email the gallery with your group name, how many people are coming, which exhibitions you would like to see, your preferred date and time, and any special needs your group has. The gallery does not say which of its two locations a given visit takes place in.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the gallery on the lower level of the library with a short spoken introduction to the exhibitions, then look at and talk about the works on display.
programs.our_note: This one sits inside a working university library, so it is quiet and there is no dedicated group space mentioned. Ask which gallery you are actually booked into when you email, because downtown and campus share the same booking address. Parking and drop off on campus are worth sorting out before the day.
programs.practical_summary: Free to walk in, on the bottom level of the library, reachable by stairs or lift although the layout can be tight for mobility devices. Washrooms, lunch space, bus drop off and group size limits are not stated for this location, so ask.
programs.evidence: We offer free exhibition introductions for university classes, school classes, and community groups of all ages.

programs.name: Indigenous Art on Campus guided walking tour
programs.description: A 90 minute guided walking tour of the Indigenous artworks sited across the UVic campus. Themes include passing on ancestral knowledge through art and story, Indigenous connections to land and place, and the interdependence of all things. The site says bookings are being taken for UVic classes, so a school or daycare group would need to ask whether they can join. A walking tour pamphlet, a video and an online map of the campus artworks are also published for people who want to do it on their own.
programs.what_children_do: Walk around the campus on foot with a guide, stopping at Indigenous artworks outdoors and hearing the stories and teachings carried by each one.
programs.our_note: This is written for university classes, so check whether they will take your group before you plan around it. It is 90 minutes outside on foot, which is a long stretch for small legs and no help in bad weather. The free pamphlet and map let you walk the same route yourself if the guided version is not available.
programs.practical_summary: Ninety minutes, outdoors, on foot across the campus, booked through the curator rather than the general gallery address. The price, the group size and whether school groups can book at all are not stated.
programs.evidence: We are now accepting bookings for 90-minute walking tours for UVic classes.

gaps: No photograph on the site is identified as the campus gallery. Every gallery photo we found is labelled as Legacy Downtown, so no main photo was recorded rather than showing the wrong building.
No street address or postal code is published for the campus gallery, only the lower level of the Mearns Centre, McPherson Library.
Opening hours are not listed. The site points to the McPherson Library hours page instead, so check that before you travel.
Washrooms, somewhere to eat and where a bus can drop off are not mentioned for the campus gallery.
No age or grade range is published for group visits. The tours page says groups of all ages, which is the only guidance given.
Group size limits, how long a visit lasts, how much notice they need and how many adults have to come are all unstated.

The two Legacy galleries, downtown and on campus, share one website, one phone number and one booking email, and the tours page does not say which gallery a group visit happens in. Worth confirming the location when you book.
The Indigenous art walking tour is written for UVic classes and no price is given, so both are worth asking about.
Workshops are listed on the site but are described as currently on hold, so no workshop was recorded.
The site's map embed gives only a map viewport rather than a published pin, so coordinates were left for geocoding from the building name.
